title: Inverse Kinematics Chain Solver with Target
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive inverse kinematics (IK) chain solver with a draggable target in 3D space.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e). Perspective camera at position (0, 5, 15) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from (5, 10, 7).
- Add a subtle grid helper (size 20, divisions 20, color 0x333355) on the XZ plane.

## IK Chain
- Create an IK chain of 5 segments (bones). Each segment is a cylinder (radius 0.15, height 2.0, color gradient from 0x00aaff for the base to 0xff5500 for the tip).
- The chain is anchored at the base position (0, 0, 0). The base joint does NOT move.
- Each joint is represented by a small sphere (radius 0.25, emissive color matching the segment).
- Joint positions array: 6 positions (base + 5 segment endpoints). Store as [{x,y,z}, ...].
- Implement the FABRIK (Forward And Backward Reaching Inverse Kinematics) algorithm:
  - Forward pass: starting from end effector, move each joint toward the previous joint at segment length distance.
  - Backward pass: starting from base (fixed), move each joint toward the next joint at segment length distance.
  - Run up to 10 iterations per frame until end effector is within 0.05 units of target or max iterations reached.
- Each joint has angle constraints: no joint can bend more than 150 degrees relative to its parent segment direction. Enforce after each FABRIK iteration.

## Target
- Create a target indicator: a glowing sphere (radius 0.4, color 0xff0044, emissive 0xff0044, emissiveIntensity 0.5) with a wireframe icosahedron around it (radius 0.6, color 0xff0044, wireframe).
- Initial target position: (3, 4, 0).
- The target can be moved via keyboard:
  - Arrow Left/Right: move target along X axis by 0.3 per press
  - Arrow Up/Down: move target along Y axis by 0.3 per press
  - Q/E keys: move target along Z axis by 0.3 per press
  - R key: reset target to initial position (3, 4, 0) and reset chain to straight-up default pose
  - Space key: toggle auto-orbit mode where target orbits in a circle (radius 4, center at (0,3,0), in XY plane, speed 1 rad/s)

## Chain Configuration UI
- Add a DOM panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, padding 15px, border-radius 8px):
  - Title: 'IK Chain Solver'
  - Display: 'Segments: 5', 'Segment Length: 2.0'
  - Display: 'End Effector Distance: X.XX' (distance from end effector to target, updated each frame)
  - Display: 'Iterations Used: N' (FABRIK iterations used in last solve)
  - Display: 'Chain Reach: X.XX' (total chain length = segments * segmentLength)
  - Display: 'Mode: Manual | Orbit' (current mode)
  - Button 'Add Segment': adds a 6th, 7th, etc. segment (max 8). New segments use interpolated color.
  - Button 'Remove Segment': removes last segment (min 2 segments).
  - Display: 'Target: (X.XX, Y.XX, Z.XX)'

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- segmentCount: number of segments (initially 5)
- segmentLength: length of each segment (2.0)
- chainReach: total reach (segmentCount * segmentLength)
- targetPosition: {x, y, z} of target
- endEffectorPosition: {x, y, z} of the last joint
- endEffectorDistance: distance from end effector to target
- iterationsUsed: FABRIK iterations used in last solve (0-10)
- jointPositions: array of {x, y, z} for each joint (length = segmentCount + 1)
- basePosition: {x, y, z} always (0, 0, 0)
- isOrbiting: boolean, whether auto-orbit is active
- orbitAngle: current orbit angle in radians (0 when not orbiting)
- converged: boolean, true if endEffectorDistance < 0.05
- maxAngle: 150 (degrees, the joint angle constraint)
- jointAngles: array of angles (in degrees) between consecutive segments (length = segmentCount - 1)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering. Ensure all numerical values are never NaN or Infinity.
physics_constraints: FABRIK algorithm must preserve segment lengths exactly (tolerance 0.001). Base joint is always fixed at origin. Joint angles must not exceed 150 degrees. End effector distance must decrease monotonically across FABRIK iterations within a single solve. Chain reach equals segmentCount * segmentLength exactly. All positions must be finite (no NaN/Infinity).
